user.title: Synkronize
user.description: Pick the media player whose artwork you want to follow, and the lights that should follow it.

data_description.media_player: The player Synkronize watches for album art.
data_description.light_entities: RGB-capable lights. Synkronize takes these over while syncing and hands them back when playback stops.

abort.already_configured: That media player and light combination is already set up.

data.idle_grace_seconds: Wait before handing the lights back

data_description.swatch: Which swatch to pull out of the artwork. Vibrant is the punchy mid-brightness color most covers have; Dominant is simply the most common color, which is often a dull background.
data_description.distribution: Spread gives each light a different color from the artwork; uniform gives them all the same one.
data_description.on_idle: Restore puts the lights back exactly as they were before syncing started.
data_description.idle_grace_seconds: How long playback may be paused or stopped before the lights are handed back. Keeps a quick pause from disturbing them.
data_description.transition: How long each color change takes on the underlying lights.
data_description.boost: How far the extracted color is pushed toward fully saturated. 0 uses it exactly as found; higher values read as more vivid on a lamp.
data_description.min_saturation: Palette colors below this saturation are not treated as vibrant. Automatically relaxed for artwork that has nothing more colorful to offer.

options.spread: Spread the palette across the lights

resync.name: Resync
resync.description: Re-download the current artwork, re-extract its colors, and re-apply them, bypassing the artwork cache.

apply_image.name: Apply image
apply_image.description: Extract colors from any image and apply them to the configured lights, ignoring the media player.

image_url.name: Image URL
image_url.description: Absolute URL of the image, or a path served by this Home Assistant instance such as /local/poster.jpg.
